items.title: Eni announces giant gas discovery offshore Indonesia

featured_image.name: Indonesia Gas Discovery at Konta-1 Dir Well in Kutai Basin ...

items.description:
Eni announced on Monday a giant gas discovery at the Geliga-1 exploration well in the Ganal block of the Kutei Basin, offshore Indonesia, with preliminary estimates pointing to in-place resources of approximately 5 trillion cubic feet of gas and 300 million barrels of condensate.[1][2]

The find adds to a string of deepwater successes for the Italian energy company in Southeast Asia and could pave the way for a third production hub in one of Indonesia's most prolific offshore basins.

items.description: The fate of Iran's enriched uranium stockpile has emerged as the central obstacle in US-Iran negotiations, with Washington demanding Tehran relinquish the material and Iran insisting it will not be "transferred anywhere" — even as a fragile ceasefire nears expiration on April 22.

items.title: 7.5-magnitude earthquake off Japan triggers tsunami warnings

featured_image.name: Japan rattled by 7.5-magnitude earthquake, tsunami warning ...

items.description:
A powerful earthquake struck off the northeastern coast of Japan on Monday afternoon, prompting tsunami warnings across several prefectures and shaking buildings as far south as Tokyo. The Japan Meteorological Agency reported the quake hit at 4:53 p.m. local time in the Pacific waters off Iwate prefecture, registering a preliminary magnitude of 7.5 at a shallow depth of about 10 kilometers below the sea surface.[1][2][3]

The JMA warned that tsunami waves of up to 3 meters could reach the northern shoreline, urging residents to evacuate immediately from coastal and riverside areas to higher ground. Tsunami warnings — the second-highest level of alert — were issued for the Pacific coasts of Iwate, Aomori, and southeastern Hokkaido, while milder advisories were posted for the coasts of Miyagi and Fukushima to the south.[4][5][1]

items.title: Samsung SDI signs first EV battery deal with Mercedes-Benz

featured_image.name: Samsung SDI in multibillion-dollar Mercedes battery deal ...

items.description:
Samsung SDI announced Monday that it has signed a multi-year agreement with Mercedes-Benz to supply batteries for the automaker's electric vehicles, marking the first time the South Korean battery maker's cells will power a Mercedes model.[1][2]

The batteries will use high-nickel NCM (nickel, cobalt, and manganese) chemistry and are destined for Mercedes-Benz's next-generation compact and mid-size electric SUVs and coupe models, Samsung SDI said in a statement. The company did not disclose the financial terms of the deal.[3][1]

items.title: UniCredit unveils plan to transform Commerzbank

featured_image.name: UniCredit to strengthen stake in Commerzbank to 30%

items.description: UniCredit is set to present its strategy for transforming Commerzbank on Monday, April 20, escalating its long-running pursuit of the German lender by publicly laying out a vision it says will make the bank "future-ready."

items.title: Oil prices surge as US Navy seizes Iranian ship near Hormuz

featured_image.name: US Navy Seizes Iranian Ship TOUSKA in Gulf of Oman

items.description: Oil prices jumped sharply on Sunday after the US Navy fired upon and seized an Iranian-flagged cargo ship attempting to bypass the American blockade of Iranian ports, capping a chaotic weekend that saw Tehran reimpose controls over the Strait of Hormuz and dash hopes of a swift reopening of the critical waterway.

items.title: Israel building permanent military bases in Gaza, satellite images show

featured_image.name: Satellite images reveal Israel expanding Gaza military sites ...

items.description: An investigation by Al Jazeera's Digital Investigations Unit, drawing on satellite imagery from Planet Labs and Sentinel Hub, has revealed that Israel is systematically building permanent military infrastructure across Gaza, even as civilian reconstruction efforts have stalled and aid organizations describe the Trump administration's ceasefire plan as a failure.

items.title: Iran adviser warns of wider sea conflict as Hormuz tightens again

featured_image.name: US Navy destroyer 'blows a hole' through Iranian cargo ship ...

items.description: Ali Akbar Velayati, a senior advisor to Iran's Supreme Leader Seyyed Mojtaba Khamenei, declared on Sunday that the era of Western powers imposing security "from across the oceans" has ended, warning that "any mischief will trigger a chain reaction." The remarks, posted on X, came as Iran doubled down on restricting maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and signaled that the conflict could extend to other global shipping chokepoints, including the Bab al-Mandeb strait off Yemen's coast.[1][2]

items.title: China tests microwave beam to recharge drones midair

featured_image.name: China demonstrates microwave beam that recharges drones in ...

items.description:
Chinese scientists have demonstrated a system that wirelessly transmits power from a ground vehicle to a drone in flight using microwave energy, a development that could one day allow unmanned aircraft to stay airborne indefinitely.

The research, published on March 25 in the peer-reviewed Chinese journal Aeronautical Science & Technology, was carried out by a team from Xidian University, an institution known for its military technology work, according to the South China Morning Post. The system uses a car-mounted microwave emitter to beam energy to an antenna array fitted to the drone's underside — and critically, it works while both the vehicle and the aircraft are moving.[1]

items.title: US-Iran talks set for Monday as ceasefire nears expiration

featured_image.name: Can Pakistan secure Iran-US nuclear compromise, as Trump ...

items.description: The fate of Iran's enriched uranium stockpile has emerged as the central obstacle in ongoing negotiations between Washington and Tehran, with President Donald Trump claiming Iran "has agreed to everything" even as Iranian officials flatly reject any transfer of nuclear material abroad. A new round of talks is expected in Islamabad on Tuesday, April 21, with a fragile ceasefire set to expire by midweek.

items.title: UAE asks U.S. for dollar swap line as Iran war strains economy

featured_image.name: Iran war wipes $120bn off Dubai, Abu Dhabi stock markets

items.description:
The United Arab Emirates has quietly initiated discussions with the United States about a potential financial safety net as the war with Iran continues to strain its economy, according to a report by The Wall Street Journal on Saturday.[1][2]

UAE Central Bank Governor Khaled Mohamed Balama raised the idea of a dollar currency-swap line with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Federal Reserve officials during meetings in Washington last week, where the Central Bank of the UAE was participating in the IMF and World Bank spring meetings. U.S. officials described the overture as precautionary rather than a formal request, with Emirati representatives stressing that they have so far managed to avoid the worst economic consequences of the conflict but may still need a backstop.[3][1]

items.title: Exit polls show Radev winning Bulgaria election by wide margin

featured_image.name: BULGARIA-VOTE

items.description:
Former Bulgarian President Rumen Radev's Progressive Bulgaria coalition is on track to win Sunday's parliamentary election by a commanding margin, exit polls showed, raising hopes of ending years of political chaos in the Balkan nation but also stoking concern over a potential shift in the country's stance toward Russia and Ukraine.

Exit surveys by the Trend research group projected Radev's center-left coalition at roughly 39% of the vote, more than double the share of his closest rival, the center-right GERB party led by longtime Prime Minister Boyko Borissov, which polled at about 15%. A separate Alpha Research exit poll broadly confirmed the result. Six parties are expected to clear the 4% threshold needed to enter the 240-seat National Assembly.[1][2][3]

items.title: Hamas signals readiness to hand over some weapons in Gaza

featured_image.name: Hamas Officials Say Group Is Ready to Hand Over Some ...

items.description: Two senior Hamas officials in Gaza have told The New York Times that the group is prepared to hand over thousands of automatic rifles and other weapons held by its police and internal security forces to a new Palestinian administrative committee, marking what could be the first concrete step toward disarmament — or a calculated attempt to deflect mounting international pressure.[1]

items.title: Trump says US seized Iranian ship as talks falter

featured_image.name: US Navy Seizes Iranian-Flagged Cargo Ship in Gulf of Oman ...

items.description: President Donald Trump announced on Sunday that American forces had captured an Iranian-flagged cargo vessel near the Strait of Hormuz, escalating tensions just as Washington pushes to restart stalled peace negotiations with Tehran. Hours later, Iran rejected the proposed second round of talks, casting fresh doubt on the prospects for a diplomatic resolution before a fragile ceasefire expires on Wednesday.

items.title: Iran refuses to negotiate while US naval blockade remains in place

featured_image.name: US general clarifies Iranian ports under blockade, not Strait of Hormuz

items.description: Iran has declared it will not send a negotiating delegation to Pakistan for a second round of peace talks with the United States as long as a US naval blockade of its ports remains in effect, according to Iran's semi-official Tasnim news agency on Sunday. The announcement throws into doubt a planned resumption of diplomacy just days before a fragile ceasefire is set to expire on April 22.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Iran refuses to send negotiators to Pakistan over US naval blockade

featured_image.name: Iran closes Strait of Hormuz again over US blockade of its ports

items.description: Iran has declared it will not send a negotiating delegation to Pakistan for a second round of peace talks with the United States as long as a US naval blockade of its ports remains in place, according to reports from Iran's semi-official Tasnim news agency on Sunday. The refusal throws into doubt plans announced by President Donald Trump, who said his representatives would arrive in Islamabad on Monday evening to resume negotiations.[1][2][3][4][5]

items.title: Trump reverses course, confirms Vance will lead Iran talks in Pakistan

featured_image.name: Vance, Witkoff, Kushner are in negotiations with Iran in Pakistan

items.description: In a confusing sequence of announcements on Sunday, President Donald Trump initially told ABC News that Vice President JD Vance would not travel to Pakistan for a second round of negotiations with Iran, only for the White House to later confirm that Vance would in fact lead the delegation. The back-and-forth unfolded as the administration scrambled to arrange talks ahead of a fragile ceasefire set to expire on Wednesday.

items.title: Pope Leo XIV prays at Angola shrine tied to slave trade

featured_image.name: TOPSHOT-ANGOLA-VATICAN-DIPLOMACY

items.description: Pope Leo XIV on Sunday led a rosary prayer at the Sanctuary of Mama Muxima, a revered Catholic shrine in Angola built by Portuguese colonizers in the late 16th century that served as a hub in the transatlantic slave trade. The visit marked one of the most symbolically charged moments of the American pope's 11-day tour of Africa.[1][2]

items.title: Trump sends envoys to Pakistan for new Iran talks

featured_image.name: Pakistan proposes second round of U.S.-Iran talks as standoff ... - PBS

items.description:
President Donald Trump announced Sunday that White House envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are heading to Islamabad for a second round of direct negotiations with Iran, with talks set to begin Tuesday, as the ceasefire between Washington and Tehran approaches its April 22 expiration.[1][2]

In an interview with Fox News, Trump warned that if Tehran does not agree to a deal, the whole of Iran will be "blown up," specifically threatening to target bridges and power plants. He demanded that Iran reopen the Strait of Hormuz and surrender its highly enriched uranium stockpile.[2][1]

items.title: U.S. backs $50M rare earth project in South Africa to cut China reliance

featured_image.name: US backs a South Africa project to extract rare earths as it ... - AP News

items.description: A U.S.-backed project in South Africa aims to extract rare earth minerals from massive industrial waste dunes, part of a broader push by Washington to loosen China's grip on the critical minerals supply chain.
